meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
meta.unit: The law fulfilled and the other sheep (3 Nephi 15–16)
principles: A law ended and prophecies kept
A saying explained because he saw they had missed it
Hearers identified as the subject of an old sentence

world_behind.title: He answers what nobody asked
world_behind.text: Verse 2 has him read the wonder on their faces about the law of Moses, and no question is recorded. The chapter is a reply to an unspoken one.

world_behind.title: The question had already split this people
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 1:24 reports men preaching that it was no more expedient to observe the law of Moses, and 1:25 has them convinced of their error in that same year. The faces in verse 2 belong to a people who argued this out thirty-three years earlier and were told the law was not yet fulfilled.

world_behind.title: The end of the law is dated by a later book
world_behind.text: 4 Nephi 1:12 says they walked no more after the performances and ordinances of the law of Moses, but after the commandments received from their Lord. The instruction in verses 4 through 8 is the moment that change begins.

world_behind.title: This is where the quoted sermon stops
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 12 through 14 track Matthew 5 through 7 closely enough to be diffed against them. This chapter has no Matthew counterpart, so from here the record carries material a reader cannot check against another book.

world_behind.title: He states what he was not commanded to say
world_behind.text: Verses 16 through 18 name the limit put on what he told those at Jerusalem, and verse 19 gives the reason: the separation was because of their iniquity.

world_behind.title: The other sheep sentence is identified
world_behind.text: Verse 21 tells them they are the people John 10:16 was about, quoting the verse back to them almost word for word.

world_behind.title: Jerusalem guessed wrong
world_behind.text: Verses 22 and 23 say they supposed he meant the Gentiles, and verse 20 has already added a third group, the other tribes, that neither side knew about.

words.text: Went up. The record uses the word nine times, five of them in this book, and the King James Bible nineteen. Verse 1 dates the sermon they just heard to before his ascension.
Continues, holds out. It appears eleven times in the record, and the King James Bible fifty-nine. Verse 9 attaches eternal life to it.
Land or property held by right of descent. The record uses the word fifty-nine times and the King James Bible two hundred and thirty-nine. Verse 13 applies it to the land they are standing on.
An enclosure for sheep, and the flock in it. Treated at Alma 5:39, of the fold of God. The word turns up fourteen times here, and the King James Bible nine, including John 10:16.
Stubbornness. Treated at 1 Nephi 2:11. Verse 18 gives it as the reason he was commanded to say no more at Jerusalem.
Set apart, divided off. The record uses the word eleven times, twice in this chapter, and the King James Bible thirty-three. Verses 19 and 20 use it of this people and of the other tribes.

phrases.term: Ye have heard the things which I taught before I ascended to my Father
phrases.text: The sermon placed in time. What they have just heard is what he taught in Judea before the resurrection.

phrases.term: They understood not the saying that old things had passed away
phrases.text: Mormon reports the confusion and Christ answers it. The question about the law of Moses is never spoken aloud.

phrases.term: I am he that gave the law, and I am he who covenanted with my people Israel
phrases.text: The claim behind the ending of the law. The one ending it is the one who gave it.

phrases.term: As many as have not been fulfilled in me... shall all be fulfilled
phrases.text: The prophets are kept. Verse 7 repeats it: an end to the old leaves untouched what is still to come.

phrases.term: The covenant which I have made with my people is not all fulfilled
phrases.text: The distinction the chapter turns on. The law has an end; the covenant does not.

phrases.term: Behold, I am the law, and the light
phrases.text: Four words that replace an institution with a person. Romans 10:4 makes the same move in different terms.

phrases.term: Ye are a light unto this people, who are a remnant of the house of Joseph
phrases.text: The twelve told what they are and whose remnant. 3 Nephi 12:14 had given the whole multitude the same word.

phrases.term: Not at any time hath the Father given me commandment that I should tell it unto your brethren at Jerusalem
phrases.text: A negative statement about revelation. He reports what he was not authorized to disclose, and to whom.

phrases.term: Other sheep I have which are not of this fold
phrases.text: The sentence quoted from John 10:16 word for word, and then explained to the people it was about.

phrases.term: They supposed it had been the Gentiles
phrases.text: Jerusalem's reading of the saying. Verse 23 gives two reasons it was wrong.

phrases.term: Ye have both heard my voice, and seen me
phrases.text: The distinguishing fact. Verse 23 had said the Gentiles would hear him only by the Holy Ghost.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: A correction prompted by a look at the crowd
verses.text: The record explains why the next nine verses exist, and the reason is an observation: "he perceived that there were some among them who marveled, and wondered what he would concerning the law of Moses; for they understood not the saying that old things had passed away." Nobody asks a question. The teaching that follows is offered because a difficulty was noticed, and the record names both the difficulty and the phrase that caused it.

verses.label: v. 4–8
verses.title: Three categories, three different statuses
verses.text: The record separates things that are usually run together. The law: "the law is fulfilled that was given unto Moses," and again "the law which was given unto Moses hath an end in me." The prophets: "I do not destroy the prophets, for as many as have not been fulfilled in me, verily I say unto you, shall all be fulfilled." The covenant: "the covenant which I have made with my people is not all fulfilled." One thing is finished, one is partly outstanding, and one is explicitly not destroyed. The distinctions are made in five verses and each is stated in its own clause.

verses.label: v. 9
verses.title: Five words that close the argument
verses.text: After the categories are sorted the record gives the identification in the shortest sentence of the chapter: "Behold, I am the law, and the light." What follows is an instruction rather than an elaboration, "Look unto me, and endure to the end, and ye shall live." Verse 10 then folds the whole of the previous section into the same claim: "this is the law and the prophets, for they truly testified of me."

verses.label: v. 14–16
verses.title: Two things not commanded, then one thing commanded
verses.text: The record states the limits before the content, and it states them as absolutes: "not at any time hath the Father given me commandment that I should tell it unto your brethren at Jerusalem"; "Neither at any time hath the Father given me commandment that I should tell unto them concerning the other tribes of the house of Israel." Only then does verse 16 give the positive, "This much did the Father command me, that I should tell unto them." A reader learns what a speaker was forbidden to say before learning what he said.

verses.label: v. 24
verses.title: The distinguishing evidence is two senses
verses.text: The chapter closes on what separates this audience from the one in Jerusalem, and it is stated physically: "ye have both heard my voice, and seen me; and ye are my sheep, and ye are numbered among those whom the Father hath given me." Hearing and sight, in that order, and the record has already reported both, the voice at 3 Ne. 11:3–6 and the sight at 3 Ne. 11:8. The claim rests on two events the book has already narrated.

chapter.title: He answers a question that was only thought
chapter.text: Verse 2 has him perceiving the puzzlement. The chapter exists because he noticed something in their faces.

chapter.title: Ending the law is not ending prophecy
chapter.text: Verses 6 and 7 make the point twice. The record is careful that "all things have become new" is not heard as a cancellation of the future.

chapter.title: The covenant outlives the law
chapter.text: Verse 8 keeps them apart in one sentence. That distinction runs through the rest of 3 Nephi.

chapter.title: The institution is replaced by a person
chapter.text: Verse 9 says he is the law and the light. Everything the law did is now located in him.

chapter.title: He describes the limits of his own commission
chapter.text: Verses 14 and 15 report what he was not commanded to say. The record is willing to show a boundary on disclosure.

chapter.title: A famous sentence gets its referent
chapter.text: Verse 21 identifies these people as the other sheep of John 10:16, and 3 Nephi 16:1 will name yet another group.

chapter.title: Misunderstanding is explained, not blamed only
chapter.text: Verse 22 gives what Jerusalem supposed and verse 23 gives what they did not know. The error is described in detail.

chapter.title: The chapter ends on evidence
chapter.text: Verse 24 says these have heard his voice and seen him. The distinction from the Gentiles is stated as a matter of fact rather than of rank.

applications.title: Answer the question people did not ask
applications.text: He saw them marvel and wonder about the law of Moses, and addressed that instead of continuing. Watch faces as well as questions, and answer the thing that is actually stopping people.

applications.title: Say what has ended and what has not, separately
applications.text: The law is ended and the covenant is not, and the sentence keeps both: "the covenant which I have made with my people is not all fulfilled." When something in your life is over, be exact about which part; a general sense that a season has closed usually takes too much with it.

applications.title: Put something in the place of what you removed
applications.text: Having ended the law he supplies the replacement in the same breath, "Behold, I am the law, and the light. Look unto me, and endure to the end." A correction that takes away a practice and leaves nothing standing where it was will not hold.

applications.title: Say what you were not authorized to say
applications.text: He reports the commandment he received, delivers it, and then reports the further thing he was told to withhold, "I was commanded to say no more." Being able to name the edge of your instructions is part of carrying them honestly.

applications.title: Notice when misunderstanding closed a door
applications.text: The reason the fuller explanation stopped was that the first hearers "understood not my word." What people fail to take in changes what they are given next. If you keep not understanding something, treat that as urgent rather than as background.

applications.title: Give people their own name in the story
applications.text: He told them they were the other sheep, and repeated the claim at verse 24, "ye are my sheep, and ye are numbered among those whom the Father hath given me." People act differently once they know which part of the account is about them.

applications.title: Sort what you have met from what you have been told
applications.text: The contrast is exact: one group did not hear the voice, and this group "have both heard my voice, and seen me." Weigh your own knowledge the same way, and do not let the second kind borrow the confidence of the first.

questions.text: What have I marveled at without asking about it?
What promise am I treating as cancelled that was only deferred?
What am I looking to instead of him?
What land or place am I treating as an inheritance?
Where has my stubbornness stopped an explanation?
What have I supposed a message meant, and been wrong?
What have I heard and seen for myself?

entries.head: 3 Ne. 1:25

anchor.quote: the law is fulfilled that was given unto Moses

entries.reason: the dispute settled thirty years earlier, the law unfulfilled

targets.quote: the law was not yet fulfilled, and that it must be fulfilled in every whit;
targets.verse_text: But it came to pass that they soon became converted, and were convinced of the error which they were in, for it was made known unto them that the law was not yet fulfilled, and that it must be fulfilled in every whit; yea, the word came unto them that it must be fulfilled; yea, that one jot or tittle should not pass away till it should all be fulfilled; therefore in this same year were they brought to a knowledge of their error and did confess their faults.
targets.markdown: But it came to pass that they soon became converted, and were convinced of the error which they were in, for it was made known unto them that **the law was not yet fulfilled, and that it must be fulfilled in every whit**; yea, the word came unto them that it must be fulfilled; yea, that one jot or tittle should not pass away till it should all be fulfilled; therefore in this same year were they brought to a knowledge of their error and did confess their faults.
